mainTopic: Preoccupation from a מצוה‎, רבן גמליאל's exceptional conduct as a mourner and with his slaves, the laws of mourning and honoring slaves, and the Sages' personal prayers after תפלה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of why a חתן marrying a בתולה is exempt from קריאת שמע. Only his kind of preoccupation counts, because it comes from a מצוה‎ (טרדא דמצוה). Ordinary worries, like an אבל's grief or a lost ship, are טרדא דרשות and do not exempt anyone. Next the משנה tells two stories about רבן גמליאל. He bathed on the night his wife died because he was an אסטניס, and he accepted תנחומין for his slave טבי because טבי was a כשר. The משנה also records a dispute over whether a חתן may choose to read קריאת שמע anyway. The גמרא explains that night-time אנינות is only דרבנן, so the רבנן did not apply it to an אסטניס. It then brings several ברייתות on slaves: no שורה, no comfort for mourners, and no הספד, and they are not called 'אבא' or 'אמא' unless they are especially important, like רבן גמליאל's slaves. The amud ends with רבי אלעזר's teaching on קריאת שמע and תפלה, followed by a list of personal prayers that great Sages said after their תפלה. רב ספרא's prayer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why only a groom marrying a virgin?
steps.stepSummary: If the groom is exempt because he is busy with a מצוה, then a man marrying an אלמנה should be exempt too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the משנה speak specifically about someone marrying a virgin? Even someone marrying a widow should also be exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason it just gave for the groom's exemption. If the reason is 'he is busy with a מצוה,' then the משנה's limit to a בתולה makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marrying an אלמנה is also a מצוה of marriage. So if 'being busy with a מצוה' is the whole reason, both grooms should be exempt. The משנה's choice of a בתולה suggests some other factor is at work.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge based on what was just said)

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not attacking the משנה's ruling. It only asks why the משנה limits the exemption to a בתולה.

phrases.english: If so
phrases.notes: Refers back to the reason given earlier: one busy with a מצוה is exempt from another מצוה.

phrases.english: why specifically one who marries a virgin?
Even one who marries a widow should also [be exempt].

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי מַאי אִירְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier reason (עוסק במצוה) given for the groom's exemption.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's restriction of the groom's exemption to one marrying a בתולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the exemption rests only on being busy with a מצוה, marrying an אלמנה is equally a מצוה, so the limit to a בתולה looks unjustified.

steps.title: The virgin's groom is preoccupied; the widow's is not
steps.stepSummary: The groom of a בתולה is anxious and preoccupied. The groom of an אלמנה is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here [with a virgin], he is preoccupied. Here [with a widow], he is not preoccupied.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the real difference is mental preoccupation. The groom of a בתולה is anxious about the marriage, while the groom of an אלמנה is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption needs two things: being involved in a מצוה and being so preoccupied that he cannot focus on קריאת שמע. Only the groom of a בתולה is preoccupied, so only he is exempt.

phrases.english: Here [one marrying a virgin], he is preoccupied,
and here [one marrying a widow], he is not preoccupied.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא טְרִיד וְהָכָא לָא טְרִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: adds the factor of mental preoccupation (טרדא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any groom, of a בתולה or an אלמנה, is exempt simply because he is involved in a מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the groom who is preoccupied, meaning the one marrying a בתולה, is exempt.

steps.title: Preoccupation alone cannot exempt: the mourner and the sunken ship
steps.stepSummary: If preoccupation exempts, then a man whose ship sank should also be exempt. Yet Rav rules that an אבל is obligated in all מצוות except תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If [the exemption] is because of preoccupation, then even someone whose ship sank at sea should also be exempt! Why, then, did רבי אבא בר זבדא say in the name of רב: A mourner is obligated in all the מצוות stated in the Torah except for תפילין, because the word 'splendor' is used about them, as it says, 'Bind your splendor upon you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. If preoccupation is the reason, then anyone with a big worry should be exempt, yet רב says an אבל, who is surely preoccupied, is still obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man whose ship just sank, or an אבל, is at least as distracted as a nervous groom. רב's ruling shows that an אבל must still keep the מצוות, including קריאת שמע. His only exemption is תפילין, and that comes from a special פסוק calling them 'splendor,' which does not suit a mourner. So preoccupation by itself does not exempt anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Splendor (a name for תפילין, from יחזקאל 24:17)

steps.confusionAlert: The תפילין exception is not based on the mourner's distraction. It comes from the word פאר: תפילין are 'splendor,' which does not fit a mourner. Everything else, including קריאת שמע, still applies to him.

phrases.english: If it is because of preoccupation,
then even one whose ship sank at sea should also [be exempt],

phrases.aramaic: אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: why then did Rabbi Abba bar Zavda say in the name of Rav:
A mourner is obligated in all the מצוות
that are stated in the Torah,
except for phylacteries,
since 'splendor' is said about them,
as it is said: 'Bind your splendor upon you, etc.'
phrases.notes: Said to יחזקאל, who was told not to mourn. This implies that a mourner does not wear תפילין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם טִרְדָּא אֲפִילּוּ טָבְעָה סְפִינָתוֹ בַּיָּם נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2 (that preoccupation is the key factor).
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that preoccupation (טרדא) is the reason for the exemption.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב rules that an אבל, who is clearly preoccupied, is obligated in all מצוות. So preoccupation alone cannot be grounds for exemption.

steps.title: Preoccupation from a מצוה versus ordinary preoccupation
steps.stepSummary: The אבל and the shipwrecked man have ordinary worries (טרדא דרשות). The groom's preoccupation comes from the מצוה itself (טרדא דמצוה).
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: There, it is preoccupation over a non-מצוה matter. Here, it is preoccupation over a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. Only preoccupation that comes from a מצוה exempts a person. Preoccupation from personal events does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both earlier ideas now combine. The groom is exempt because he is involved in a מצוה and is also preoccupied by that מצוה. The mourner and the shipwrecked man are distracted by events that are not מצוות, so they stay obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: Preoccupation over a voluntary, non-מצוה matter

steps.whatToRemember: A חתן of a בתולה is exempt from קריאת שמע only because his preoccupation comes from a מצוה‎ (טרדא דמצוה). Ordinary distress, like mourning or financial loss (טרדא דרשות), does not exempt anyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a lasting principle: being distracted is not an excuse from מצוות unless the distraction itself comes from a מצוה.

phrases.english: They say:
There it is preoccupation over a voluntary matter,
here it is preoccupation over a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי הָתָם טִרְדָּא דִרְשׁוּת הָכָא טִרְדָּא דְמִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by distinguishing two types of preoccupation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: refines the type of preoccupation that counts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any preoccupation, such as grief or financial loss, should exempt a person.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only preoccupation that comes from a מצוה‎ (טרדא דמצוה) exempts. Ordinary preoccupation (טרדא דרשות) does not.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל bathes on the night his wife died
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells that רבן גמליאל bathed on the first night after his wife died. When his students challenged him, he explained that he is an אסטניס, a delicate person.
steps.simpleTranslation: He bathed on the first night after his wife died. His students said to him: Didn't you teach us, our teacher, that a mourner may not bathe? He said to them: I am not like other people. I am delicate.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a story about רבן גמליאל acting differently from the normal rule for an אבל, and gives his own explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אבל is normally not allowed to bathe. רבן גמליאל does not say the rule is wrong. He says he is a special case, because for an אסטניס, not bathing causes real physical suffering.

keyTerms.meaning: A delicate, sensitive person who suffers physically without bathing

phrases.english: MISHNA: He bathed on the first night
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבן גמליאל, continuing the stories from earlier in the משנה

phrases.english: after his wife died.
His students said to him:
Did you (not) teach us, our teacher,
that a mourner is forbidden to bathe?
He said to them:
I am not like other people,
I am delicate.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רָחַץ לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁמֵּתָה אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the גמרא's discussion of the חתן's exemption back to the text of the משנה, which continues with stories about רבן גמליאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אסטניס who is an אבל may bathe on the first night, because he is an exception to the mourning rule against bathing.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל accepts condolences for his slave טבי
steps.stepSummary: When his slave טבי died, רבן גמליאל accepted תנחומין. When his students challenged him, he explained that טבי was a כשר, a virtuous person.
steps.simpleTranslation: When his slave טבי died, he accepted condolences for him. His students said to him: Didn't you teach us, our teacher, that we do not accept condolences for slaves? He said to them: My slave טבי is not like all other slaves. He was a virtuous man.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second story in the משנה with the same pattern. רבן גמליאל seems to break his own rule, and he explains why this case is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal rule is that people do not accept תנחומין over the death of slaves. רבן גמליאל keeps that rule. He treats טבי as an exception because of his outstanding righteousness.

keyTerms.meaning: רבן גמליאל's slave, known for his righteousness

phrases.english: And when Tavi, his slave, died,
he accepted condolences for him.
His students said to him:
Did you (not) teach us, our teacher,
that one does not accept condolences for slaves?
He said to them:
Tavi my slave is not
like all the other slaves,
he was virtuous.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁמֵּת טָבִי עַבְדּוֹ קִבֵּל עָלָיו תַּנְחוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 5: the students challenge his conduct, and he explains why his case is an exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Normally one does not accept תנחומין for slaves, but an exceptionally virtuous slave like טבי may be honored this way.

steps.title: May a groom choose to read קריאת שמע on his wedding night?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says a חתן who wants to read קריאת שמע on the first night may do so. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees: not everyone may claim a reputation for piety.
steps.simpleTranslation: A groom who wants to read קריאת שמע on the first night may read it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Not everyone who wants to take the name may take it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a disagreement about a חתן who is exempt from קריאת שמע but wants to read it anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חתן is exempt because he is busy with the מצוה of marriage. The תנא קמא lets him read voluntarily. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says this would be showing off, since he is not really able to concentrate and only looks pious.

keyTerms.meaning: To take the name, meaning to claim a reputation for piety

steps.confusionAlert: The groom is not forbidden in principle. The question is whether he may go beyond his exemption. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל worries it looks like יוהרא, arrogant display.

phrases.english: A groom, if he wishes to recite
Shema on the first night —
he may recite.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Not everyone who wishes
to take the name (of piety) may take it.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָתָן אִם רוֹצֶה לִקְרוֹת קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹרֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of the חתן's exemption, which was discussed in steps 1–4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, a groom may voluntarily read קריאת שמע. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, he should not, since it is a display of false piety.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the later discussion of when one may take on a stricter practice and when it counts as showing off (יוהרא).

steps.title: Why was רבן גמליאל allowed to bathe?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the legal reason behind רבן גמליאל bathing as a mourner.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבן גמליאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks what legal reasoning allowed רבן גמליאל to bathe on the night his wife died. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'I am delicate' explains his feelings, but not why the halacha allows it. The גמרא wants the legal basis for the exception.
steps.confusionAlert: The words in parentheses (שמעון בן) are a printer's correction and should be removed. The question is about רבן גמליאל from the bathing story, not רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from the חתן case.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason
of Rabban Gamliel?
phrases.notes: The parenthetical words are deleted. This refers to רבן גמליאל who bathed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first story in the משנה (step 5) to explain it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The halachic basis that allowed an אבל who is an אסטניס to bathe on the first night.

steps.title: Mourning at night is only rabbinic, and the רבנן did not decree on a delicate person
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל holds that אנינות applies מדאורייתא only on the day of death, learned from the words כיום מר. The night after is only דרבנן, and the רבנן did not apply their decree to an אסטניס.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that mourning at night is only rabbinic, as it says: 'and its end like a bitter day.' And for a delicate person, the רבנן did not make their decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question in step 8. It explains that the night's mourning is only rabbinic, so the רבנן could make room for an אסטניס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'like a bitter day,' which shows that the Torah-level אנינות is only by day. The following night is a rabbinic extension. Since the רבנן made that rule, they never meant it to cover someone for whom it would cause real physical suffering.

keyTerms.meaning: The acute first stage of mourning, before burial or on the day of death

steps.whatToRemember: Torah-level אנינות is only by day ('כיום מר'). The night is דרבנן, and the רבנן did not apply their decree to an אסטניס. That is why רבן גמליאל could bathe.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general principle: a rabbinic rule can be relaxed for someone who would suffer real physical distress from it, while a Torah rule cannot be relaxed so easily.

phrases.english: He holds:
acute mourning at night is rabbinic,
as it is written: 'and its end like a bitter day.'
phrases.notes: 'Day' shows that the Torah-level mourning is only by day.

phrases.english: And in the case of a delicate person
the Rabbis did not decree upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר אֲנִינוּת לַיְלָה דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אנינות at night is only rabbinic, based on 'כיום מר', and the rabbinic decree was never applied to an אסטניס.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the משנה about טבי and brings a ברייתא on mourning for slaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about טבי, then brings a ברייתא: for slaves and maidservants we do not stand in a שורה, and we say neither ברכת אבלים nor תנחומי אבלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה said: 'When טבי his slave died, etc.' The רבנן taught: For slaves and maidservants, we do not stand in a row for them, and we do not say the mourners' blessing or the mourners' comfort for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about טבי, and brings a ברייתא with the basic rule for mourning slaves. This is the background rule that רבן גמליאל departed from when he accepted תנחומין for טבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when someone dies, people form a שורה (row) to comfort the mourners and say special words of comfort. The ברייתא says these do not apply when a slave dies. On the surface, this seems to clash with רבן גמליאל accepting תנחומין for טבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaves and maidservants (non-Jewish servants owned by a Jewish master)
The row of comforters who stand and console the mourners after the burial
The special blessing said for mourners
The words of comfort said to mourners

steps.confusionAlert: The first line is not a new statement. It is the גמרא quoting the משנה so we know which part it is now discussing: the story of טבי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the background rule. It explains why רבן גמליאל's students were surprised, and why he had to say that טבי was special, a כשר.

phrases.english: And when Tavi his slave died, etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה. It marks the topic now being discussed.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
phrases.notes: Introduces a ברייתא.

phrases.english: Slaves and maidservants:
we do not stand in a row for them,
phrases.notes: The comforters' row after a burial.

phrases.english: and we do not say the mourners' blessing for them
or the mourners' comfort.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת אֵין עוֹמְדִין עֲלֵיהֶם בְּשׁוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבן גמליאל's bathing (Steps 8-9), the גמרא now turns to the טבי story from Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The standard mourning rituals (שורה, ברכת אבלים, תנחומי אבלים) are not done for slaves and maidservants.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר runs away from students who come to comfort him
steps.stepSummary: When רבי אליעזר's maidservant died, his students came to comfort him. He kept moving from room to room, and they kept following him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A story: רבי אליעזר's maidservant died. His students came in to comfort him. When he saw them, he went up to the upper floor, and they went up after him. He went into the gatehouse, and they went in after him. He went into the big hall, and they went in after him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a story that shows the rule from Step 10 in real life. This step sets up the scene. רבי אליעזר's rebuke comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר was hinting, without words, that he did not want to receive תנחומין for a maidservant. The students missed the hint each time and kept following him. This builds toward his sharp comment in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident brought to teach a halacha

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה וּמֵתָה שִׁפְחָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.english: There was an incident: Rabbi Eliezer's maidservant died.
His students came in to comfort him.
As soon as he saw them, he went up to the upper floor,
phrases.notes: His first hint that he did not want comfort.

phrases.english: and they went up after him.
He went into the gatehouse; they went in after him.
He went into the hall; they went in after him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה וּמֵתָה שִׁפְחָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life story that shows the rule of Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר avoided receiving תנחומין for his maidservant.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר rebukes his students and repeats the rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר tells his students they missed every hint, and reminds them that he taught them that we do not comfort mourners for slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I thought you would get burned even by lukewarm water. Now I see you do not get burned even by boiling hot water! Did I not teach you this: For slaves and maidservants, we do not stand in a row for them, and we do not say the mourners' blessing or the mourners' comfort for them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר finally says out loud what he was hinting: you should not be comforting me for a maidservant. He quotes the same rule from the ברייתא in Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Burned by lukewarm water' means getting a small hint. 'Not burned even by boiling water' means missing even a very strong hint. The story shows that the rule in Step 10 was taught and practiced by a great תנא, רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: It seems to me / I thought
Burned by lukewarm water: picking up a small hint
Boiling hot water: a very strong hint

phrases.english: He said to them:
I thought that you would get burned by lukewarm water,
phrases.notes: I thought you would understand a small hint.

phrases.aramaic: עַכְשָׁיו אִי אַתֶּם נִכְוִים אֲפִילּוּ בְּחַמֵּי חַמִּין,
phrases.english: now you are not burned even by boiling hot water!
phrases.notes: You missed even an obvious hint.

phrases.english: Did I not teach you this:

phrases.aramaic: עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת אֵין עוֹמְדִים עֲלֵיהֶם בְּשׁוּרָה,
phrases.english: Slaves and maidservants: we do not stand in a row for them,
and we do not say the mourners' blessing for them
nor the mourners' comfort?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא כָּךְ שָׁנִיתִי לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The climax of the story from Step 11: רבי אליעזר explains his behavior.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that we do not do שורה, ברכת אבלים, or תנחומי אבלים for slaves.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's behavior and his own words to his students.

steps.title: So what do we say when a slave dies?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks: if not the usual comfort, what do we say when a slave dies?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what do we say about them?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבי אליעזר asks a question so he can teach the correct thing to say in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule so far only told us what NOT to do. This question opens the positive side: there is still something proper to say to the owner.

phrases.english: Rather, what do we say about them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מָה אוֹמְרִים עֲלֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After saying what not to do, he asks what we should do instead.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What words are proper to say to an owner whose slave died?

steps.title: We say 'May המקום fill your loss,' as for an animal
steps.stepSummary: Just as we say 'המקום ימלא לך חסרונך' to someone whose ox or donkey died, we say the same about his slave or maidservant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as we say to a person about his ox or his donkey that died, 'May המקום fill your loss,' so too we say to him about his slave or maidservant, 'May המקום fill your loss.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers his own question. For a slave, we say the same words we say for a lost animal: 'May המקום fill your loss.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner's link to a slave is treated as a financial loss, not a family loss. So he gets words for a loss, not the comfort given to a mourner. This explains why the usual mourning rituals do not apply.
steps.whatToRemember: For slaves we do not do the usual mourning comforts. We only say 'המקום ימלא לך חסרונך', the same as for a lost animal, because it is treated as a financial loss.

phrases.english: Just as we say to a person
about his ox and about his donkey that died:
"May the Omnipresent fill your loss,"

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אוֹמְרִים לוֹ עַל עַבְדּוֹ וְעַל שִׁפְחָתוֹ
phrases.english: so too we say to him about his slave and about his maidservant:
"May the Omnipresent fill your loss."

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאוֹמְרִים לוֹ לְאָדָם עַל שׁוֹרוֹ וְעַל חֲמוֹרוֹ שֶׁמֵּתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We say 'המקום ימלא לך חסרונך', the same words used for a dead ox or donkey.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: no eulogy for slaves, but רבי יוסי allows praise for a good slave
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says we do not eulogize slaves. רבי יוסי says that for an עבד כשר we may say: 'Alas, a good and loyal man who enjoyed the fruit of his labor.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: We do not eulogize slaves and maidservants. רבי יוסי says: If he was a virtuous slave, we say about him: 'Alas, a good and faithful man, who enjoyed the work of his own hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא about a הספד (eulogy) for slaves. The first opinion says no eulogy at all. רבי יוסי allows a short praise if the slave was a כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new idea: a special category of 'עבד כשר', a virtuous slave, who might deserve more honor. This connects to רבן גמליאל's answer in the משנה, that טבי was a כשר.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יוסי's idea of an עבד כשר helps us understand רבן גמליאל's answer in the משנה: טבי was a special exception because he was a כשר.

phrases.english: Another baraita taught:
Slaves and maidservants: we do not eulogize them.
Rabbi Yosei says:
If he is a virtuous slave,
we say about him:
"Alas, a good and faithful man,
who enjoyed the fruit of his labor."
phrases.notes: He lived off his own honest work.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת אֵין מַסְפִּידִין אוֹתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from comforting the owner to eulogizing the slave, and adds רבי יוסי's exception for an עבד כשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First opinion: no הספד for slaves. רבי יוסי: an עבד כשר may receive a short praise.

steps.title: The חכמים object: that praise is too high for a slave
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say to רבי יוסי: if you give such praise to a slave, what is left to say for truly virtuous people?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: If so, what have you left for the virtuous people?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יוסי. They say his praise is too big for a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'a good and faithful man who lived from his own work' would be fine praise even for a respected Jew. If we say it for a slave, there is no higher praise left for the truly כשרים. So the חכמים reject even this small eulogy.
steps.whatToRemember: No הספד for slaves. רבי יוסי allows praise for an עבד כשר, but the חכמים say that praise is too high, because it would leave nothing more for truly virtuous people.

phrases.english: They said to him:
If so, what have you left for the virtuous?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question that works as a challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִם כֵּן, מָה הִנַּחְתָּ לַכְּשֵׁרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוסי's ruling from Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's ruling that an עבד כשר gets the praise 'הוי איש טוב ונאמן ונהנה מיגיעו'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That praise fits even honored, virtuous Jews. Giving it to a slave leaves no higher praise for the truly כשרים.

steps.title: Only three are called fathers, only four are called mothers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the title אבות is only for three people and the title אמהות is only for four.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: We only call three people 'the Fathers' (אברהם, יצחק, יעקב), and we only call four people 'the Mothers' (שרה, רבקה, רחל, לאה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that limits who may be called אבות and אמהות. This is background that will lead into a rule about how we address slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The title 'father' or 'mother' of the nation is an honor. The ברייתא says it stops with אברהם, יצחק and יעקב. The twelve tribes, like ראובן and שמעון, do not get it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Matriarchs: שרה, רבקה, רחל, לאה
We do not call (someone by a title)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a sudden change of topic. The rule about who earns the title 'father' prepares for the next ברייתא, which asks whether slaves may be called 'אבא'.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
We call only three people 'Fathers',
phrases.notes: אברהם, יצחק, יעקב

phrases.english: and we call only four people 'Mothers'.
phrases.notes: שרה, רבקה, רחל, לאה

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין קוֹרִין ״אָבוֹת״ אֶלָּא לִשְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of eulogies and moves to a related topic: honorific titles. This prepares the ground for the rule about calling slaves 'אבא'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only three people are called אבות and only four are called אמהות.

steps.title: Why only three fathers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind limiting the title אבות to three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding the Fathers: what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the sons of יעקב are not also called אבות. This question sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The twelve tribes are also our ancestors, so it seems they should be called 'fathers' too. The גמרא wants the reason they are left out.

phrases.english: The Fathers: what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָבוֹת מַאי טַעְמָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ברייתא in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the title אבות stops at יעקב and does not include his sons.

steps.title: Suggested reason: we don't know which tribe we come from
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that we cannot call any tribe 'our father' because we do not know whether we descend from ראובן or שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because we do not know whether we come from ראובן or from שמעון...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible reason with the word אילימא, 'if you say'. That word warns us the idea is about to be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that calling someone 'our father ראובן' might be false, since most people do not know their tribe. Only אברהם, יצחק and יעקב are surely ancestors of every Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will likely be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say it is because we do not know
whether we come from Reuben
or whether we come from Simon,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא יָדְעִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first, tentative answer to the question in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Tentative: the tribes are not called אבות because we do not know which tribe we descend from.

steps.title: That reason fails for the mothers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: we also do not know whether we come from רחל or לאה, yet both are called אמהות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, for the Mothers too we do not know whether we come from רחל or from לאה! (Yet we still call them Mothers.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the reason from step 19 by showing it does not match the rule about the אמהות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If uncertain descent blocked the title, רחל and לאה should lose it too, since most people do not know which of them they come from. But the ברייתא counts them among the four אמהות. So uncertainty cannot be the real reason.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי אִמָּהוֹת נָמֵי לָא יָדְעִינַן
phrases.english: If so, regarding the Mothers too we do not know
whether we come from Rachel
or whether we come from Leah!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי אִמָּהוֹת נָמֵי לָא יָדְעִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested reason of step 19.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same uncertainty applies to רחל and לאה, yet they are still called אמהות.

steps.title: Real reason: only they are important enough
steps.stepSummary: The real reason is importance: up to יעקב they are important enough for the title, and beyond him they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: until here (יעקב) they are important; beyond that, they are not important enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. The title depends on importance, not on knowing who you descend from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלא, 'rather', drops the old reason and brings a new one. The title 'father of the nation' is an honor kept for the most important figures, the three אבות and four אמהות. This idea of 'חשיבות' will be the key to the slaves question that comes next.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of 'importance' (חשיבות) set up here is the same idea the גמרא uses at the end to explain רבן גמליאל's slaves.

phrases.english: Rather, up to here they are important,
beyond that they are not important (enough).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, עַד הָכָא חֲשִׁיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason of step 19 with the accepted reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The title is limited to the most important figures. The אבות and אמהות are important enough, and the later generations are not.

steps.title: Slaves are not called 'אבא' or 'אמא', except רבן גמליאל's
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא: slaves and maidservants are not called 'אבא so-and-so' or 'אמא so-and-so'. But רבן גמליאל's slaves were called that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: slaves and maidservants are not called 'Father so-and-so' and 'Mother so-and-so'. But the slaves of רבן גמליאל were called 'Father so-and-so' and 'Mother so-and-so'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that applies the honorific idea to slaves. It gives a rule and then a story that seems to go against it, which sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People often called respected older people 'אבא' or 'אמא' as a title of honor. The ברייתא says slaves do not get this title. Then it reports that in רבן גמליאל's home, his slaves did get it.

phrases.english: It was taught in another baraita:
Slaves and maidservants, we do not call them
'Father so-and-so' and 'Mother so-and-so'.

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָיוּ קוֹרִים אוֹתָם
phrases.english: But those of Rabban Gamliel, they would call them
'Father so-and-so' and 'Mother so-and-so'.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידָךְ: עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת אֵין קוֹרִין אוֹתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the idea of honorific titles from steps 17-21 and returns to the main theme of how slaves are treated (steps 12-16).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaves and maidservants are not given the titles 'אבא' or 'אמא', yet רבן גמליאל's slaves were.

steps.title: How can a story contradict the rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does the ברייתא bring a story that contradicts the rule it just taught?
steps.simpleTranslation: A story to contradict the rule?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. Normally a story is brought to support a rule, not to break it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said slaves are not called 'אבא'. Then it told of slaves who were called 'אבא'. It looks like the ברייתא is fighting with itself, and the גמרא demands an explanation.

phrases.english: A story to contradict?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה לִסְתּוֹר?!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inner consistency of the ברייתא in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story of רבן גמליאל's slaves inside the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story should illustrate the rule. Here the story seems to show the opposite of the rule.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's slaves were especially important
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. רבן גמליאל's slaves were called 'אבא' and 'אמא' because they were important.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they were important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. The story is an exception because these slaves were especially important.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule stands: ordinary slaves do not get the honorific title. רבן גמליאל's slaves were distinguished people, so they earned it. This uses the same measure of 'importance' that explained the אבות.
steps.whatToRemember: Titles like 'אבות' or 'אבא' depend on importance (חשיבות). Only three אבות and four אמהות get the national title. Ordinary slaves are not called 'אבא'/'אמא', but important slaves like those of רבן גמליאל can be.

phrases.english: Because they were important.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דַּחֲשִׁיבִי.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the story is a special exception, not a contradiction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story seemed to contradict the ברייתא's rule about slaves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies to ordinary slaves. רבן גמליאל's slaves were important, so they received the title as an exception.

steps.title: A verse hinting at קריאת שמע and תפלה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the first half of the verse refers to קריאת שמע and the second half refers to תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: What does the verse 'So I will bless You as I live, to Your name I will raise my hands' mean? 'So I will bless You as I live' is קריאת שמע. 'To Your name I will raise my hands' is תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רבי אלעזר takes one verse and splits it into two halves: one half for קריאת שמע and one half for תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each half of the verse is matched to a different daily מצוה. Raising one's hands is a picture of standing before ה׳ and asking, so it fits תפלה. This sets up the reward that comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? (a standard opening for explaining a verse)
Prayer; here it means the עמידה (שמונה עשרה)
I will raise my hands (a picture of praying)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"So I will bless You as I live,
phrases.notes: Psalms 63:5

phrases.english: to Your name I will raise my hands"?
"So I will bless You as I live"
this is the recitation of Shema.
"To Your name I will raise my hands"
this is prayer (the Amida).
phrases.notes: Lifting hands is a picture of standing before ה׳ in prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New aggadic topic. It does not continue the discussion of slaves being called אבא and אמא in steps 22-24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verse 'כן אברכך בחיי בשמך אשא כפי' refers first to קריאת שמע and then to תפלה.

steps.title: The reward for saying שמע and praying
steps.stepSummary: One who does both קריאת שמע and תפלה is satisfied 'as with fat and marrow' and inherits both this world and עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person does this, the next verse speaks about him: 'As with fat and marrow my soul will be satisfied.' And more than that, he inherits two worlds, this world and עולם הבא, as it says: 'With lips of joys my mouth praises.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר continues and describes the reward for someone who does both מצוות from the last step. He brings the next verse to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Fat and marrow' is a picture of being fully satisfied. The word 'רננות' (joys) is plural, so it is read as two joys: the joy of this world and the joy of עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Fat and marrow; a picture of rich, full satisfaction
And not only that, but even more
Joys; plural, so it hints at two joys

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, saying קריאת שמע and davening תפלה together earns reward in both this world and עולם הבא.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof for 'two worlds' is not a clear statement in the verse. It comes from the plural form רננות, 'joys', which is read as two joys.

phrases.english: And if one does so (says Shema and prays),
about him the verse says:
"As with fat and marrow, my soul will be satisfied."
phrases.notes: Psalms 63:6

phrases.english: And not only that, but
he inherits two worlds:
this world and the World-to-Come,
as it is stated:
"With lips of joys my mouth will praise."
phrases.notes: Joys (plural) means two joys: this world and the World-to-Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם עוֹשֶׂה כֵּן עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אלעזר's statement by adding the reward for doing what step 25 described.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who says קריאת שמע and davens is fully satisfied and inherits this world and עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's personal prayer after davening
steps.stepSummary: After his תפלה, רבי אלעזר asked for love and peace, many students, a good end, a share in גן עדן, a good friend, a good יצר, and fear of Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: After finishing his prayer, רבי אלעזר said: May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that You place love, brotherhood, peace, and friendship among us. Give us many students, and give us a good end and hope. Put our portion in גן עדן, and give us a good friend and a good יצר in Your world. May we wake up and find our hearts longing to fear Your name, and may our soul's wishes come before You for good.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tells us what extra prayer רבי אלעזר said after finishing the עמידה. This begins a list of such personal prayers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits with step 25: the same רבי אלעזר who praised תפלה added his own requests at the end of it. His prayer covers relationships, Torah students, a good ending, עולם הבא, and serving ה׳ with a full heart.

keyTerms.meaning: May it be Your will (the usual opening of a personal request)
The satisfaction of our souls; our deep wishes

steps.whyThisMatters: This and the next prayers show that a person may add personal requests after the עמידה. This is the background for the 'אלקי נצור' style prayers said today.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, after he finished his prayer,
said this:
"May it be Your will, Lord our God,
that You cause to dwell in our lot
love and brotherhood, peace and friendship.
And may You fill our borders with many students
and make our end successful, with a good future and hope.
And place our portion in the Garden of Eden,

phrases.aramaic: וְתַקְּנֵנוּ בְּחָבֵר טוֹב וְיֵצֶר טוֹב בְּעוֹלָמֶךָ.
phrases.english: and provide us with a good friend and a good inclination in Your world.
And may we rise early and find our hearts longing
to fear Your name,
and may the satisfaction of our souls come before You for good."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בָּתַר דִּמְסַיֵּים צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי אלעזר's teaching about תפלה to the personal prayer he himself said after תפלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר added a personal prayer for peace, students, a good end, גן עדן, good companionship, and fear of Heaven.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's personal prayer after davening
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asked ה׳ to see our shame and trouble and to act toward us with mercy, strength, kindness, grace, goodness, and humility.
steps.simpleTranslation: After finishing his prayer, רבי יוחנן said: May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that You look at our shame and see our trouble. Dress Yourself in Your mercy, cover Yourself with Your strength, wrap Yourself in Your kindness, and tie on Your grace. May Your quality of goodness and Your humility come before You.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second example: the prayer רבי יוחנן said after finishing his תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר asked for specific good things. רבי יוחנן instead asks ה׳ to treat us with His kind qualities. Each phrase is a picture of ה׳ putting on a garment of mercy, strength, kindness, or grace.
steps.confusionAlert: Words like 'clothe Yourself' and 'gird Yourself' are pictures, not physical descriptions. They are a way of asking ה׳ to act toward us with these qualities.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan, after he finished his prayer,
said this:
"May it be Your will, Lord our God,
that You look at our shame and see our trouble,
and clothe Yourself in Your mercy, and cover Yourself with Your strength,
and wrap Yourself in Your kindness, and gird Yourself with Your grace,
and may Your quality of goodness and Your humility come before You."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בָּתַר דִּמְסַיֵּים צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second entry in the list of personal prayers said after תפלה, following רבי אלעזר's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן asked ה׳ to look at our troubles and treat us with mercy, strength, kindness, grace, goodness, and humility.

steps.title: רבי זירא's short prayer after davening
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asked that we not sin and not be put to shame before our forefathers.
steps.simpleTranslation: After finishing his prayer, רבי זירא said: May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that we not sin, not be ashamed, and not be disgraced before our forefathers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third example: רבי זירא's short prayer after his תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's prayer is short and focuses on one thing: not sinning. He asks that our actions never bring shame on the good ways of our forefathers.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר, רבי יוחנן, and רבי זירא each added their own personal prayer after the עמידה. This shows that adding personal requests at the end of תפלה is a long-standing practice.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira, after he finished his prayer,
said this:
"May it be Your will, Lord our God,
that we not sin and not be ashamed,
and not be disgraced before our forefathers."
phrases.notes: Our actions should not shame the good deeds of our forefathers.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא בָּתַר דִּמְסַיֵּים צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third entry in the list of personal prayers said after תפלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא prayed that we not sin and not bring shame on our forefathers.

steps.title: רבי חייא's prayer: תורה as our life's work
steps.stepSummary: After his תפלה, רבי חייא asked that Torah be our main occupation, that our heart not grow faint, and that our eyes not grow dim.
steps.simpleTranslation: After רבי חייא prayed, he said: 'May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that Your Torah be our profession, that our heart not grow weak, and that our eyes not grow dark.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another Sage's personal prayer to the list. This one is from רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא wants Torah to be his real 'job,' not a side activity. He also asks for the strength to keep going: a heart that does not give up and eyes that do not dim, whether from sadness or from long hours of learning.

keyTerms.meaning: 'May it be (Your) will.' The standard opening of a personal request to ה׳.
Our profession or trade. Here it means our main occupation.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בָּתַר דִּמְצַלֵּי אָמַר הָכִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya, after he prayed, said this:
"May it be Your will, ה׳ our God,
that Your Torah be our profession,
and may our heart not grow faint,
and may our eyes not grow dim."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בָּתַר דִּמְצַלֵּי אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of private prayers after תפלה that began with רבי אלעזר, רבי יוחנן, and רבי זירא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא prayed that Torah be his life's work and that he have the emotional and physical strength to keep at it.

steps.title: רב's prayer for a long and full good life
steps.stepSummary: After his תפלה, רב asked for a long life filled with peace, goodness, blessing, a livelihood, health, fear of sin, honor, love of Torah, and fulfillment of the heart's good wishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: After רב prayed, he said: 'May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that You give us long life: a life of peace, of goodness, of blessing, of livelihood, of physical vigor, a life with fear of sin, a life without shame or disgrace, a life of wealth and honor, a life in which we love Torah and fear Heaven, a life in which You fulfill all our heart's requests for good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב's personal prayer after תפלה. It is a long list, and each line begins with the word 'life.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב does not only ask for a long life. He asks that the life be filled with both physical blessings (livelihood, health, wealth) and spiritual ones (יראת חטא, אהבת תורה, יראת שמים). Even the request for wealth and honor sits right next to the request to love Torah. The last line asks that our wishes be fulfilled only 'לטובה', meaning only if they are truly good for us.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'strengthening of the bones.' It means physical vigor and good health. (Sefaria translates it as freedom of movement.)
Fear of sin: being careful not to do wrong
The requests or wishes of our heart

steps.whyThisMatters: This prayer is familiar. With small additions, it is the יהי רצון we say in shul on the שבת before ראש חודש, at ברכת החודש.

phrases.english: Rav, after his prayer, said this:
"May it be Your will, ה׳ our God,
that You give us long life,

phrases.aramaic: חַיִּים שֶׁל שָׁלוֹם, חַיִּים שֶׁל טוֹבָה,
phrases.english: a life of peace, a life of goodness,

phrases.aramaic: חַיִּים שֶׁל בְּרָכָה, חַיִּים שֶׁל פַּרְנָסָה,
phrases.english: a life of blessing, a life of livelihood,
a life of physical vigor,
phrases.notes: Literally 'strengthening of the bones.'

phrases.english: a life that has fear of sin in it,
a life that has no shame or disgrace in it,
a life of wealth and honor,

phrases.aramaic: חַיִּים שֶׁתְּהֵא בָּנוּ אַהֲבַת תּוֹרָה וְיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם,
phrases.english: a life in which we have love of Torah and fear of Heaven,

phrases.aramaic: חַיִּים שֶׁתְּמַלֵּא לָנוּ אֶת כָּל מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבֵּנוּ לְטוֹבָה״.
phrases.english: a life in which You fulfill for us all the requests of our heart for good."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the next Sage's personal prayer to the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב prayed for a long life that is full of both material and spiritual good.

steps.title: רבי's prayer to be saved from arrogance and harm
steps.stepSummary: After his תפלה, רבי יהודה הנשיא asked to be saved from arrogant people and from arrogance, and from bad people, bad events, a bad יצר, bad friends and neighbors, the destroying שטן, and harsh judgments and opponents, whether Jewish or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: After רבי prayed, he said: 'May it be Your will, ה׳ our God and God of our fathers, that You save us from brazen people and from brazenness, from a bad person and a bad mishap, from the bad inclination, a bad friend, a bad neighbor, the destroying שטן, a harsh judgment, and a harsh opponent in court, whether he is a member of the covenant or not.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the personal prayer of רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא). Unlike רב, who asked for good things, רבי asks to be protected from bad things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's list moves from dangers outside a person (arrogant people, bad neighbors, harsh opponents) to dangers inside a person (arrogance itself, the יצר הרע). He asks for protection from a harsh opponent in a lawsuit, whether that person is Jewish (בן ברית) or not.

keyTerms.meaning: Brazenness and arrogance as a trait, in others or in oneself
A bad mishap or harmful event
A harsh opponent in a lawsuit
Member of the covenant, meaning a Jew

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב (step 31) with רבי (this step). 'רבי' with no name always means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה. 'רב' is a later Babylonian אמורא.
steps.whyThisMatters: We still say this prayer every morning. It is the יהי רצון at the start of שחרית, in the morning ברכות.

phrases.english: Rebbi, after his prayer, said this:

phrases.aramaic: ״יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ,
phrases.english: "May it be Your will, ה׳ our God and God of our fathers,
that You save us from brazen people and from brazenness,
from a bad person, and from a bad mishap,
from the bad inclination, from a bad friend,
from a bad neighbor, and from the destroying Satan,
and from a harsh judgment and from a harsh opponent in court,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁהוּא בֶּן בְּרִית בֵּין שֶׁאֵינוֹ בֶּן בְּרִית״.
phrases.english: whether he is a member of the covenant or not a member of the covenant."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another Sage's personal prayer. This one focuses on protection instead of blessings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי prayed to be protected from arrogance and from many kinds of outside and inside harm.

steps.title: רבי prayed this even though royal guards protected him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי said this prayer for protection even though royal officers stood guard over him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said this even though royal officers stood guard over רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short note about רבי's prayer from the previous step. It points out something surprising: he already had bodyguards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי was the leader of the Jews and was close to the Roman government, so officers protected him. You might think such a person has no need to pray for protection from bad people. The גמרא teaches that he still prayed, because human protection is not enough and a person must still turn to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: Officers or guards (here, royal officers protecting רבי)

steps.whatToRemember: The Sages each added their own personal prayer after the עמידה. Two of them are still in our סידור: רב's prayer at ברכת החודש and רבי's prayer in the morning ברכות. Even רבי, who had royal guards, still asked ה׳ for protection.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקָיְימִי קָצוֹצֵי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי.
phrases.english: And this was even though officers stood guard over Rebbi.
phrases.notes: The word עליה ('over him') is followed by דרבי ('of רבי'), which spells out who is being guarded.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקָיְימִי קָצוֹצֵי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on רבי's prayer from step 32 and highlights how unexpected it was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even with human protection, רבי still prayed every day to be saved from harm and arrogance.

steps.title: רב ספרא's prayer after his תפלה begins with a request for peace
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces the personal prayer that רב ספרא said after his תפלה. It opens with "יהי רצון" and asks ה׳ to establish peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: After his prayer, רב ספרא said this: "May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that You establish peace..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is adding another sage, רב ספרא, to its list of people who said a personal prayer after תפלה. This line only opens his prayer, and the request for peace continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier prayers of רבי זירא, רבי חייא, רב and רבי, this one also uses the standard opening "יהי רצון מלפניך". רב ספרא's very first request is for שלום, and the next words will explain where he wants that peace to be.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose personal prayer is quoted here
After his prayer (after finishing the עמידה)
May it be Your will — the standard opening of a personal request

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the end of the prayer. The sentence is cut off in the middle, and the next part of the text tells us where רב ספרא asks for peace to be established.

phrases.english: Rav Safra, after his prayer,
phrases.notes: Same formula used for the earlier sages in this list.

phrases.english: said this:
"May it be Your will
Lord our God,
that You establish peace
phrases.notes: The request continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב סָפְרָא בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sages' personal prayers after תפלה, moving from רבי's prayer (and the note about his guards) to רב ספרא's prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ספרא's personal prayer after תפלה opens with a request that ה׳ establish peace.
